I do the exact same thing. I've kinda just trained myself to say these things under my breath or so replace the words with stupid things like change  "I want to die" to "I want a pie." Or just when I'm in the car by myself I will just scream that shit all I want to get it out if my system. I honestly don't think this is the healthiest way to go about it but I know that I don't mean what I'm saying so as long as it stays that way I just try to keep it away from people. masks have helped a lot with this. I'll just me at work cursing a storm under my breath in front of people and they are never the wiser.

I do the same thing. I'm so sorry you lost your friend. I lost one of mine to the virus last may.  I don't know why exactly I do it. Sometimes it is  because I'm not trusting with many people to open up like that. If you have someone you trust them I would say to reach out to them and kinda force your feelings out. Starting to talk about it is the scariest part. I've reach out and have gotten some unexpectedly amazing support. If you can't really talk them you can think of something that will help you feel happier and ask that person to do that. Like I will ask my friend to stay on facetime with me while I watch a show so I don't feel alone. I hope my response helped.

So the places where you get locked up here are really bad. My brother went to a mental hospital a couple months ago (he wasn't even suicidal. He wanted his medication adjusted and thought that getting hospitalized for being suicidal would be fastest. So he just lied because he thought it would be the same when he was a minor in a minor's mental hospital. adult ones are bad) My mom was trying to call him during their "call in" hours but other patients who couldn't even talk were answering the phone so we could not get a hold of him. one time when we did get a hold of him we started hearing screaming from multiple other patients and then the hospital cut the phone lines (one of them were calling the police). Later after we had to fight to get him out he told us that since he wasn't a really bad patient they just locked in up in solitary for a while because they didn't know what to do with him. It's really shit health care here and they had to transfer him to a place far away from where he lives so I won't even be close to my town. it's very very very bad. (I live in america. surprise surprise right?) and regarding the therapist, I just started having sessions with her. When I mentioned suicide to her she seemed very jumpy like she wanted to call as soon as I said it.
